catalyst_text: Received UK MHRA authorization for Phase 1/2 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: A Phase 1/2 study of mRNA-4194 for Lynch syndrome received UK MHRA authorization. This clearance enables initiation of the trial to assess safety, immune responses, and dose selection in a high-risk population.
catalyst_text_evidence: The University of Oxford and Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today announced a Phase 1/2 study of mRNA-4194, Moderna's investigational mRNA-based cancer vaccine for Lynch Syndrome, has received Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) authorization in the UK.

catalyst_text: Positive Phase 3 results published and PDUFA set
detailed_catalyst_text: Peer-reviewed Phase 3 results for a seasonal influenza vaccine were published in NEJM, showing superior relative vaccine efficacy versus a standard-dose comparator in adults 50 years and older, including those 65+. Regulatory filings were accepted in the U.S., Europe, Canada, and Australia, and the FDA assigned a PDUFA goal date of 2026-08-05. This reflects strong efficacy evidence and active regulatory review toward potential approvals.
catalyst_text_evidence: Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today announced a publication in the New England Journal of Medicine of the positive Phase 3 study results evaluating mRNA-1010, its vaccine candidate for seasonal influenza. As previously reported, mRNA-1010 achieved the most stringent superiority criterion prespecified in the protocol, with an rVE of 26.6% (95% CI; 16.7%, 35.4%) in the overall study population. mRNA-1010 has been accepted for regulatory review in the U.S., Europe, Canada and Australia. Moderna has received a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) goal date of 2026-08-05.

drug_indication: Influenza and COVID-19 prevention in adults 50+
catalyst_text: Received European Commission marketing authorization for combination vaccine
detailed_catalyst_text: The European Commission granted marketing authorization for a flu plus COVID-19 combination vaccine for adults 50 years and older. The authorization is valid across all EU member states as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway, enabling national access processes. This approval provides a single-dose option that can simplify immunization against both viruses.
catalyst_text_evidence: the European Commission (EC) has granted marketing authorization for mCOMBRIAX (mRNA-1083), the Company’s mRNA combination vaccine for active immunization for the prevention of influenza disease and COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2 in individuals 50 years of age and older. This marketing authorization follows the positive opinion from the European Medicines Agency’s (EMA) Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) and is valid in all 27 European Union member states, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway.

drug_indication: Checkpoint Inhibitor Refractory Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma, PD-L1 Positive
catalyst_text: Received FDA Fast Track designation for melanoma
detailed_catalyst_text: Received FDA Fast Track designation for the combination in checkpoint inhibitor refractory unresectable or metastatic melanoma with PD-L1 positive tumors. This designation allows more frequent FDA interactions and potential rolling review to expedite development and evaluation.
catalyst_text_evidence: The U.S. FDA has granted Fast Track designation for mRNA-4359 in combination with pembrolizumab for the treatment of CPI refractory unresectable or metastatic melanoma with PD-L1+ (TPS>1%).

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 2 cohort results in melanoma
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported Phase 2 dose-expansion results from a Phase 1/2 study in first-line locally advanced or metastatic melanoma, showing an ORR of 83% (2 complete responses, 8 partial responses) and a DCR of 92% among 12 patients, with a median time to response of six weeks. Antigen-specific T-cell responses were observed and safety was manageable with no new immune-related adverse events. These findings support continued development of the regimen in melanoma.
catalyst_text_evidence: The presentation reports safety, efficacy and translational data from a Phase 2 dose-expansion cohort of the Phase 1/2 study (NCT05533697), which evaluated mRNA-4359 + pembrolizumab as a first-line therapy in patients with locally advanced or metastatic melanoma. Among 12 participants, mRNA-4359 + pembrolizumab resulted in an overall response rate (ORR) of 83% (95% CI: 52%-98%), with two patients achieving a complete response and eight achieving a partial response, as well as a disease control rate (DCR) of 92% (95% CI: 62%-100%). mRNA-4359 + pembrolizumab demonstrated a manageable safety profile, with no new immune-related adverse events (AEs).

catalyst_text: Received EU approval for COVID 19 prevention
detailed_catalyst_text: The European Commission granted marketing authorization for the vaccine for active immunization against COVID-19 in individuals 12 years and older across the European Union and associated countries. It is the third product authorized in the region, reinforcing the respiratory vaccine portfolio.
catalyst_text_evidence: Moderna, Inc. today announced that the European Commission (EC) has granted marketing authorization for mNEXSPIKE (mRNA-1283), a new COVID vaccine, for active immunization to prevent COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2 in individuals aged 12 years and older. This marketing authorization is valid in all 27 European Union Member States, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. This marketing authorization follows the positive opinion adopted by the European Medicines Agency's (EMA) Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) and marks Moderna's third product authorized in the European Union, alongside Spikevax and mRESVIA, further strengthening the Company's respiratory vaccine portfolio in Europe.

catalyst_text: Received Refusal to File letter from FDA
detailed_catalyst_text: The U.S. FDA’s CBER issued a Refusal-to-File letter for the BLA of the investigational seasonal influenza vaccine, citing the choice of a standard-dose comparator and noting no specific safety or efficacy concerns. Regulatory submissions for this vaccine have been accepted for review in the EU, Canada, and Australia, indicating active reviews outside the U.S.
catalyst_text_evidence: Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) has notified the Company that it will not initiate a review of the biologics license application (BLA) for its investigational influenza vaccine, mRNA-1010, and has issued a Refusal-to-File (RTF) letter. CBER's RTF letter, signed by Center Director Vinayak Prasad, MD, MPH, identified the choice of a licensed standard-dose seasonal influenza vaccine comparator as the sole reason for the refusal to initiate the review of Moderna's application. The letter did not identify any specific safety or efficacy concerns regarding mRNA-1010. mRNA-1010 has been accepted for review in the EU, Canada and Australia.

catalyst_text: Submitted marketing applications in US EU Canada Australia
detailed_catalyst_text: Applications for marketing authorization were submitted to FDA, EMA, Health Canada, and Australia’s TGA for a seasonal influenza vaccine for adults aged 50 and older. Filings are supported by positive Phase 3 data showing efficacy across age groups and a favorable safety profile. This advances the program toward potential approvals across multiple major markets.
catalyst_text_evidence: "The Company has filed for marketing authorization with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the European Medicines Agency (EMA), Health Canada, and the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) in Australia." "Moderna, Inc. (NASDAQ:MRNA) today provided an update on regulatory submissions for its investigational seasonal influenza vaccine, mRNA-1010, for adults aged 50 years and older." "The regulatory applications are based on positive data from multiple Phase 3 studies. In a Phase 3 efficacy study (P304), mRNA-1010 achieved the most stringent superiority criterion prespecified in the protocol, with a relative vaccine efficacy (rVE) of 26.6% (95% CI; 16.7%, 35.4%) across all adults aged 50 years and older."
